title: Why nature is good for your brain, with Marc Berman, PhD

sentences.en: When you're stressed or overwhelmed, do you ever just go for a walk to clear your head?
sentences.zh: 当您感到压力山大或不堪重负时，您会去散散步来清醒一下头脑吗？

sentences.en: Many of us feel intuitively that nature is good for us.
sentences.zh: 我们许多人凭直觉感到大自然对我们有益。

sentences.en: We know that spending time outside among trees or near the water can help us feel calmer, clearer, and more focused.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，在树林中或水边度过时光可以帮助我们感到更加平静、思路更清晰、注意力更集中。

sentences.en: Now, a growing body of research is proving our intuitions right.
sentences.zh: 如今，越来越多的研究正在证明我们的直觉是正确的。

sentences.en: Psychologists and other researchers have found that access to nature is critical to people's mental and physical health.
sentences.zh: 心理学家和其他研究人员发现，接触大自然对人们的身心健康至关重要。

sentences.en: And in an age of constant distractions, they're also finding that spending time in nature can help us recapture our powers of focus and concentration.
sentences.zh: 在这个充满各种干扰的时代，他们还发现，置身于大自然中可以帮助我们重新找回专注力和注意力。

sentences.en: So what is it about natural environments that is so beneficial for our brains?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么自然环境对我们的大脑如此有益呢？

sentences.en: Do we need to spend time in unspoiled forests or on hiking trails to see these effects?
sentences.zh: 我们需要花时间去未受破坏的森林或远足小径才能看到这些效果吗？

sentences.en: Or can city trees and parks work just as well?
sentences.zh: 还是说城市的树木和公园也能起到同样的作用？

sentences.en: What can you do to interior spaces like your home to make them feel more natural?
sentences.zh: 你可以对家里等室内空间做些什么，让它们感觉更自然？

sentences.en: What if you're not an outdoorsy person?
sentences.zh: 如果你不是一个喜欢户外活动的人怎么办？

sentences.en: Do you have to enjoy spending time in nature to benefit from it?
sentences.zh: 你必须喜欢在大自然中度过时光才能从中受益吗？

sentences.en: And what implications does this research have for policymakers, urban planners, and others who shape our physical world?
sentences.zh: 这项研究对政策制定者、城市规划者以及其他塑造我们物理世界的人有什么启示？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到《心理学话语》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理学科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: My guest today is Dr. Mark Berman, a professor of psychology at the University of Chicago, where he heads the Environmental Neuroscience Laboratory.
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾是芝加哥大学心理学教授马克·伯曼博士，他在那里领导环境神经科学实验室。

sentences.en: Dr. Berman's research uses brain imaging, behavioral experiments, and other methods to explore how
sentences.zh: 伯曼博士的研究利用脑成像、行为实验和其他方法来探索

sentences.en: our physical environments, especially nature, affect our attention, memory, and emotion.
sentences.zh: 我们的物理环境，尤其是大自然，是如何影响我们的注意力、记忆力和情绪的。

sentences.en: His work has been featured in media outlets, including CNN, NPR, the New York Times, the Wall
sentences.zh: 他的工作曾在 CNN、NPR、《纽约时报》、《华尔街日报》和《华盛顿邮报》等

sentences.en: Street Journal, and the Washington PoSt.
sentences.zh: 媒体上报道。

sentences.en: His new book is called Nature and the Mind, the science of how nature improves cognitive, physical, and social well-being.
sentences.zh: 他的新书名为《自然与心灵：自然如何改善认知、身体和社交健康的科学》。

sentences.en: Dr. Berman, thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 伯曼博士，谢谢你今天加入我的节目。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me on the program.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你邀请我参加这个节目。

sentences.en: I want to start with a study you published back in 2008.
sentences.zh: 我想从你在 2008 年发表的一项研究开始。

sentences.en: As you explain in your book, this was an experiment that helped pave the way for basically all your future research, and it has to do with just taking a walk in a park.
sentences.zh: 正如你在书中解释的那样，这是一项为你的几乎所有未来研究铺平道路的实验，它与在公园里散步有关。

sentences.en: Tell us about that study and what you found.
sentences.zh: 给我们讲讲那项研究以及你发现了什么。

sentences.en: Yeah, so that study was one of the first studies in kind of environmental psychology that looked to see if interacting with nature changed people's attention and their memory
sentences.zh: 是的，所以这项研究是环境心理学中首批探讨与大自然互动是否能改变人们注意力和记忆力的研究之一

sentences.en: using kind of objective measures.
sentences.zh: 通过使用某种客观指标。

sentences.en: So often people who did these studies in the past, they would kind of just ask people, did you feel better after the walk in nature?
sentences.zh: 所以过去做这些研究的人经常只是问人们，你在大自然中散步后感觉好点了吗？

sentences.en: And most people said, yes, they felt better.
sentences.zh: 大多数人都说，是的，他们感觉好多了。

sentences.en: But we took a more sort of quantitative approach to say, okay, but does nature actually change our working memory and attention performance?
sentences.zh: 但我们采取了一种更具量化水平的方法来探讨，好吧，大自然真的会改变我们的工作记忆和注意力表现吗？

sentences.en: So I designed a study with two of my mentors, Steve Kaplan and John Janitas.
sentences.zh: 所以我与我的两位导师史蒂夫·卡普兰和约翰·雅尼塔斯共同设计了一项研究。

sentences.en: And basically what we did is we gave participants a challenging attention and working memory task called the backwards digit span task.
sentences.zh: 基本上我们做的是让参与者完成一项具有挑战性的注意力和工作记忆任务，称为倒序数字广度任务。

sentences.en: And that was a task where you would hear digits out loud, like four, eight, three, and you need to repeat them back in backwards order.
sentences.zh: 这是一个大声听到数字的任务，比如四、八、三，你需要按倒序重复它们。

sentences.en: So three, eight, four.
sentences.zh: 也就是三、八、四。

sentences.en: And three digits, the task is pretty easy, but we keep increasing the number of digits all the way up to about nine digits.
sentences.zh: 如果是三个数字，这个任务很简单，但我们不断增加数字的数量，一直增加到大约九个数字。

sentences.en: At around five digits, the task is pretty hard.
sentences.zh: 在大约五个数字时，任务就相当难了。

sentences.en: So we gave participants this backwards digit span task, and then we gave them a map to go on a walk in a more natural environment.
sentences.zh: 所以我们让参与者完成这个倒序数字广度任务，然后给他们一张地图，让他们在更自然的自然环境中散步。

sentences.en: This was the Ann Arbor Arboretum near the University of Michigan campus, or we had people walk on a more urban path down busy Washtenaw Avenue in Ann Arbor.
sentences.zh: 这是密歇根大学校园附近的安娜堡植物园，或者我们让人们在安娜堡繁忙的华盛顿大道沿着更具都市感的路线散步。

sentences.en: Both walks were about 2.6 miles, and it took participants about 50, 5-0 minutes to complete
sentences.zh: 两次散步都在 2.6 英里左右，参与者大约花了 50 分钟来完成

sentences.en: the walk, and then after the walk, they returned to the lab and they took this backwards digit span task again.
sentences.zh: 散步，然后散步结束后，他们回到实验室，再次参加这个倒序数字广度任务。

sentences.en: We also did two important things too before participants went on the walk.
sentences.zh: 在参与者去散步之前，我们也做了两件重要的事情。

sentences.en: So one thing is we gave participants a GPS watch so that we could track them.
sentences.zh: 所以其中一件事是，我们给了参与者一块 GPS 手表，以便我们能够追踪他们。

sentences.en: So we made sure that they didn't just go to Starbucks, that they actually went on the walk.
sentences.zh: 所以我们确保他们不只是去了星巴克，而是真正去散步了。

sentences.en: And then we also used the GPS traces to make sure that people didn't get lost because we thought if people got lost, maybe the walk wouldn't be very beneficial.
sentences.zh: 然后我们还使用 GPS 轨迹来确保人们不会迷路，因为我们认为如果人们迷路了，散步可能就不会那么有益了。

sentences.en: They might be too stressed out.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会压力太大。

sentences.en: And then we also took participants' cell phones.
sentences.zh: 然后我们还收走了参与者的手机。

sentences.en: So we kept their cell phones in the lab.
sentences.zh: 所以我们将他们的手机留在实验室里。

sentences.en: We didn't want them sort of chit-chatting and texting on the walk.
sentences.zh: 我们不希望他们在散步时闲聊和发短信。

sentences.en: We wanted them to be really, really engaged with the natural environment or the urban environment when they went on those walks.
sentences.zh: 我们希望他们在散步时能够真正地、全情投入到自然环境或城市环境中。

sentences.en: So participants, they take this backwards digit span task, then they either go for a walk in nature or they go for a walk in an urban environment.
sentences.zh: 所以参与者完成这个倒序数字广度任务，然后他们要么去大自然中散步，要么去城市环境中散步。

sentences.en: They come back to the lab, they take this backwards digit span task again, and then they return to the lab a week later and repeat the whole procedure again.
sentences.zh: 他们回到实验室，再次参加这个倒序数字广度任务，然后一周后他们回到实验室，重复整个流程。

sentences.en: But if they walked in the natural environment the first week, they walk in the urban environment the second week or vice versa.
sentences.zh: 但如果他们在第一周在自然环境中散步，他们就会在第二周在城市环境中散步，反之亦然。

sentences.en: So everybody was their own control.
sentences.zh: 所以每个人都是自己的对照组。

sentences.en: And what we found was pretty amazing that participants improved by about 20% on this difficult
sentences.zh: 我们发现的结果非常惊人，参与者在完成这项困难的

sentences.en: attention and memory task, this backwards digit span task, after they walked in nature.
sentences.zh: 注意力和记忆力任务（这个倒序数字广度任务）时，在大自然中散步后提高了大约 20%。

sentences.en: But they really didn't show any improvement after they went on the urban walk.
sentences.zh: 但他们在城市散步后并没有表现出任何改善。

sentences.en: And we thought, wow, this is a pretty cool finding.
sentences.zh: 我们想，哇，这是一个非常酷的发现。

sentences.en: That's quite significant.
sentences.zh: 这相当显著。

sentences.en: So let me ask you, why did this work?
sentences.zh: 所以请问，为什么这会起作用？

sentences.en: Why would just taking a walk in a park as opposed to on city streets help people do better on a cognitive test?
sentences.zh: 为什么仅仅在公园里散步而不是在城市街道上散步就能帮助人们在认知测试中表现得更好？

sentences.en: Well, we think it has to do with attention.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们认为这与注意力有关。

sentences.en: And I mentioned that I did this work in collaboration with Stephen Kaplan and John Janitis.
sentences.zh: 我提到过我与史蒂夫·卡普兰和约翰·雅尼塔斯合作完成了这项工作。

sentences.en: And Steve Kaplan had developed a theory called attention restoration theory that basically posits
sentences.zh: 史蒂夫·卡普兰提出了一种名为“注意力恢复理论”的理论，该理论基本上认为

sentences.en: that humans have two kinds of attention and that our attention could be kind of restored or replenished with different kinds of physical environments.
sentences.zh: 人类有两种注意力，并且我们的注意力可以通过不同类型的物理环境得到某种恢复或补充。

sentences.en: So one kind of attention that Steve posited that humans have is called directed attention.
sentences.zh: 史蒂夫提出人类拥有的一种注意力被称为定向注意力。

sentences.en: And that's the kind of attention that we use at work or at school where you as an individual person are deciding what you're paying attention to.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们在工作或学校中使用的注意力，即作为个体的你决定自己正在关注什么。

sentences.en: And it's thought that that kind of attention is fatigable or depletable, that you can only sort of direct your attention for so long before you become mentally fatigued.
sentences.zh: 人们认为这种注意力是容易疲劳或消耗的，你在精神疲劳之前只能定向集中注意力一段时间。

sentences.en: And it's hard to pay attention anymore.
sentences.zh: 而且很难再集中注意力。

sentences.en: And we've all had that sensation like at the end of a long workday where you might be looking
sentences.zh: 我们都有过这种感觉，就像在漫长的工作日结束时，你可能正看着

sentences.en: at the computer screen and you're just kind of staring at the screen and you're not able to get anything done.
sentences.zh: 电脑屏幕，然后你只是盯着屏幕发呆，什么也做不成。

sentences.en: You're kind of mind wandering.
sentences.zh: 你的思维有点开小差。

sentences.en: It's hard to focus.
sentences.zh: 很难集中注意力。

sentences.en: That's what we call a directed attention fatigue state.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们所说的定向注意力疲劳状态。

sentences.en: That's when we think it would be a good time to take a break.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们认为休息一下的好时机。

sentences.en: That's different from involuntary attention, which is the kind of attention that we think is automatically captured by interesting stimulation in the environment.
sentences.zh: 这不同于非随意注意力，这种注意力被认为会自动被环境中有趣的刺激所吸引。

sentences.en: So bright lights, loud noises, those things automatically capture our attention.
sentences.zh: 所以亮光、巨响，这些东西会自动吸引我们的注意力。

sentences.en: And it's thought that that's sort of less susceptible to fatigue or depletion.
sentences.zh: 人们认为这不太容易疲劳或耗尽。

sentences.en: So you don't often hear people say, oh, I can't look at that beautiful waterfall anymore.
sentences.zh: 所以你不会经常听到有人说，哦，我再也无法看那个美丽的瀑布了。

sentences.en: It's just so breathtaking.
sentences.zh: 它太壮观了。

sentences.en: I'm too tired.
sentences.zh: 我太累了。

sentences.en: I can't look at it anymore.
sentences.zh: 我再也看不了了。

sentences.en: Oh, I can't watch this really interesting movie anymore.
sentences.zh: 哦，我再也不能看这部非常有趣的电影了。

sentences.en: It's just too interesting.
sentences.zh: 它太有趣了。

sentences.en: I'm too tired.
sentences.zh: 我太累了。

sentences.en: I have to shut it off.
sentences.zh: 我必须把它关掉。

sentences.en: So the idea with attention restoration theory is that if we can find environment that don't
sentences.zh: 因此，注意力恢复理论的理念是，如果我们能找到一个对定向注意力

sentences.en: place a lot of demands on directed attention, while simultaneously having interesting stimulation
sentences.zh: 没有太多要求的环境，同时又有有趣的刺激来激活非随意注意力，我们就可以恢复这种宝贵的定向注意力资源。

sentences.en: to activate the involuntary attention, we could kind of restore this precious directed attention resource.
sentences.zh: 我们认为自然环境就是能做到这一点的环境之一。

sentences.en: And we think that natural environments are one kind of environment that can do this.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着大自然是唯一能做到这一点的环境。

sentences.en: It doesn't mean that nature is the only environment that can do this.
sentences.zh: 但我们认为许多自然环境，比如你当地的公园，在那里你感到安全，那里有有趣的东西可看，你不需要对定向注意力提出太多要求，但它们有有趣的刺激来激活非随意注意力。

sentences.en: But we think that many natural environments think your local park, where you feel safe, where there's interesting things to look at, you don't have to place a lot of demands on
sentences.zh: 还有一件事我也想提一下，那就是我们认为你的非随意注意力是如何被激活的很关键。

sentences.en: directed attention, but they have interesting stimulation to activate the involuntary attention.
sentences.zh: 所以我们认为这种刺激应该是柔和迷人的，而不是严厉迷人的。

sentences.en: There's one other thing, too, that I want to mention also, which is that we think it's important how your involuntary attention is activated.
sentences.zh: 为了再次解释这一点，如果你看到一个美丽的瀑布，它会吸引你的注意力，但它并没有真正吸引你所有的注意力焦点。

sentences.en: So we think that it's important that the stimulation be softly fascinating and not harshly fascinating.
sentences.zh: 当你看着这个美丽的瀑布时，你可以开小差并思考其他事情。

sentences.en: So to kind of explain that again, if, if you see a beautiful waterfall, it captures your attention, but it doesn't really capture all of your attentional focus.
sentences.zh: 当我在时代广场时，它也非常有趣，有大量的刺激来吸引我的非随意注意力。

sentences.en: You can kind of mind wander and think about other things while you're looking at this beautiful waterfall.
sentences.zh: 但它以一种吞噬一切的方式做到这一点，以至于我，你知道的，我真的无法思考任何其他事情。

sentences.en: When I'm in Times Square, it's also really interesting, lots of stimulation to capture my involuntary attention.
sentences.zh: 我们并不认为这种注意力吸引是令人放松的。

sentences.en: But it sort of does so in an all consuming way where I, where, you know, I can't really think about anything else.
sentences.zh: 所以我们认为吸引你注意力的刺激需要是柔和迷人的。

sentences.en: And we, we don't think that that kind of attentional capture is restful.
sentences.zh: 同样，自然环境往往具有柔和迷人的刺激。

sentences.en: So we think that the kind of stimulation that captures your attention needs to be softly fascinating.
sentences.zh: 这主要关乎视觉刺激吗？

sentences.en: And again, natural environments tend to have softly fascinating stimulation.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当你置身于大自然中时发生的其他事情呢，无论是气味还是声音、鸟鸣？

sentences.en: And is it mostly about the visual stimulation?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这会如何影响你的注意力？

sentences.en: I mean, what about the other things that are happening when you're in nature, whether that smells or sounds, bird calls?
sentences.zh: 是的，我们认为这绝对是多模态的。

sentences.en: I mean, how, how might that affect your attention?
sentences.zh: 所以当你真正去大自然中散步时，你会得到视觉、嗯，听觉刺激。

sentences.en: Yeah, we think it's definitely multimodal.
sentences.zh: 你可能会得到触觉刺激。

sentences.en: So when you're, when you're actually out on the real walk in nature, you're getting the visual, uh, you're getting the auditory stimulation.
sentences.zh: 你可能会得到嗅觉、气味刺激。

sentences.en: You might be getting the tactile stimulation.
sentences.zh: 所以所有这些事情都在发挥作用。

sentences.en: You might be getting the olfactory, the smell stimulation.
sentences.zh: 我们做过这样的研究，向人们展示大自然的图片或自然视频，其中

sentences.en: So it's all, all those things are at play.
sentences.zh: 只有视觉刺激，特别是图片，我们发现你可以获得一些

sentences.en: We have done studies where we show people just pictures of nature or nature videos and where
sentences.zh: 类似的好处，仅仅看着大自然的图片与城市景色的图片相比，这表明大自然的视觉模式有其独到之处。

sentences.en: it's just visual stimulation, uh, in particular, the pictures, and we find you can get some
sentences.zh: 但我们也让人们聆听自然声音与城市声音，我们在那里得到了类似的好处。

sentences.en: similar benefits, just looking at pictures of nature versus pictures of urban scenes, which suggests that it's something about the visual patterns of nature.
sentences.zh: 所以，大自然的声学特性、熵、频谱轮廓，可能有些东西更容易被我们的大脑处理。

sentences.en: But we've also had people listen to nature sounds versus urban sounds and we get similar benefits there.
sentences.zh: 我们尚未测试嗅觉属性。

sentences.en: So there, there's something about the acoustic properties of nature, the entropy, the spectral profile, uh, that might be easier for our brains to process.
sentences.zh: 虽然我有一位同事莱斯利·凯，她是嗅觉专家，她一直在跟我谈论萜烯，

sentences.en: We haven't yet tested the olfactory, uh, properties.
sentences.zh: 这是一种在大自然气味中发现的分子化合物，主要是美好的大自然气味，也许摄入萜烯有什么奇效，但我们更多地关注视觉和听觉，部分原因在于这更容易。

sentences.en: Although I have a colleague, Leslie Kay, who's a expert on olfaction and she's been talking to
sentences.zh: 嗯，但所有这些不同的模态都有可能在起作用。

sentences.en: me about terpenes, uh, this molecular compound that's found in nature smells and primarily good
sentences.zh: 重要的是，你知道的，尽管我们发现看大自然图片和听自然声音有效果，我认为这很重要，因为很多人无法

sentences.en: nature smells, maybe there's something about ingesting terpenes, but we've focused more on the visual and the auditory in part because it's easier.
sentences.zh: 轻易接触大自然。

sentences.en: Um, but it's possible that all of these different modalities are at play.
sentences.zh: 我们不认为这可以替代真正的自然。

sentences.en: And importantly, you know, even though we find effects of looking at pictures of nature and listening to nature sounds, which I think is important because lots of people don't have

sentences.en: nature and, um, nature sounds suggest that there's something about the aesthetic of nature or the perceptual properties of nature that might contribute.
sentences.zh: 大自然以及，嗯，自然的声音表明，大自然的美学或大自然的感知特性可能起到了作用。

sentences.en: So for example, uh, natural stimulation visually has like higher fractalness, um, than urban stimulation.
sentences.zh: 所以举个例子，嗯，视觉上的自然刺激具有更高的分形度，嗯，比城市刺激要高。

sentences.en: And what I mean by fractalness is, uh, if you imagine, imagine a snowflake, it's got a shape, a characteristic shape.
sentences.zh: 我所说的分形度是，嗯，如果你想象一下，想象一片雪花，它有一种形状，一种特征形状。

sentences.en: And if you put that snowflake under the microscope, under a microscope and zoomed in, you would see some of the same shape.
sentences.zh: 如果你把这片雪花放在显微镜下，在显微镜下放大，你会看到一些相同的形状。

sentences.en: And if you zoomed in even more, you would see some of that same shape that it doesn't matter what scale, what spatial scale you look at the snowflake.
sentences.zh: 如果你放大更多，你会看到同样的一些形状，无论你以什么比例，什么空间比例去看这片雪花。

sentences.en: It's got the same characteristic shape.
sentences.zh: 它都有相同的特征形状。

sentences.en: So that's called fractal, uh, or scale free that it doesn't matter what scale you look at the stimulus.
sentences.zh: 所以这被称为分形，嗯，或者无标度，也就是说你以什么比例去看刺激物并不重要。

sentences.en: It's got the same characteristic shape and nature is kind of filled with this fractal or scale free stimulation.
sentences.zh: 它具有相同的特征形状，大自然可以说是充满了这种分形或无标度的刺激。

sentences.en: So you can imagine a tree, a tree has got a trunk that branches out into big branches that branch out into smaller branches,
sentences.zh: 所以你可以想象一棵树，一棵树有一个主干，分叉成大树枝，再分叉成更小的树枝，

sentences.en: which branches out into smaller branches, which branches out into leaves.
sentences.zh: 树枝再分叉成更小的树枝，最后分叉成树叶。

sentences.en: Then the veins have leaves that, you know, veins that branch out.
sentences.zh: 然后叶子的叶脉，你知道的，叶脉也在分叉。

sentences.en: There's the same kind of branching structure at different scales of the tree.
sentences.zh: 在树木的不同尺度上，都有着同一种分叉结构。

sentences.en: And people really like looking at fractal, uh, stimulation.
sentences.zh: 人们非常喜欢看分形，嗯，刺激。

sentences.en: And it may be also the case that, um, our brains might process that stimulation more, more fluently.
sentences.zh: 而且也可能是，嗯，我们的大脑处理这种刺激会更流畅，更加流畅。

sentences.en: And whether you're looking at a forest or an ocean scene, um, they both tend to have some of the same fractal, uh, kind of structure to them.
sentences.zh: 无论你是看着森林还是海洋的景色，嗯，它们往往都具有一些相同的分形，嗯，那种结构。

sentences.en: And we think there are similar things happening with the sound.
sentences.zh: 我们认为声音方面也发生了类似的事情。

sentences.en: So, you know, bird song waves crashing, these natural sounds tend to have some of the same
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，鸟鸣声、海浪拍打声，这些自然的声音往往具有一些相同的

sentences.en: acoustic properties that we think our brains might process more, more fluently compared to some other kinds of stimulation you'd find in an urban environment.
sentences.zh: 声学特性，我们认为与你在城市环境中发现的一些其他刺激相比，我们的大脑处理起来可能会更流畅、更顺畅。

sentences.en: Like imagine a car horn honking or a car alarm going off.
sentences.zh: 就像想象汽车喇叭声或汽车警报器响起一样。

sentences.en: Nobody would say that that kind of acoustic stimulation is pleasant to listen to or, or really restful to, to listen to.
sentences.zh: 没有人会说那种声学刺激听起来很悦耳，或者听起来真的很让人放松。

sentences.en: Is there a certain amount of time you need to spend in nature to get these benefits?
sentences.zh: 你需要花一定的时间在大自然中才能获得这些益处吗？

sentences.en: And, and does it matter if it's in a really wild environment or maybe you're just in a manicured garden?
sentences.zh: 而且，这是否取决于它是在一个非常野生的环境中，还是你可能只是在一个修剪整齐的花园里？

sentences.en: Yeah, those are really, really great questions.
sentences.zh: 对，这些真的是非常非常棒的问题。

sentences.en: And unfortunately, my short answer is we don't know everything yet about that.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，我简短的回答是，我们对此还并非完全了解。

sentences.en: There's still a lot of work to be done.
sentences.zh: 还有很多工作要做。

sentences.en: There has been research to suggest that in terms of interacting with nature, how much would you need to interact to get the benefits?
sentences.zh: 有研究表明，就与大自然互动而言，你需要互动多少才能获得益处？

sentences.en: Some people say you want to interact with nature about two hours a week.
sentences.zh: 有些人说你每周需要与大自然互动大约两个小时。

sentences.en: We've found that the 50 minute walk in nature works, but people have found that shorter walks in nature could work like 30 minutes or 20 minutes.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，在大自然中散步50分钟是有效的，但人们发现较短时间的自然散步也能起作用，比如30分钟或20分钟。

sentences.en: When we have people view the pictures of nature, that's for about 10 minutes.
sentences.zh: 当我们让人观看大自然的照片时，时间大约是10分钟。

sentences.en: Same thing for listening to nature.
sentences.zh: 听大自然的声音也是如此。

sentences.en: We had people listen to nature for about 10 minutes.
sentences.zh: 我们让人听大自然的声音大约10分钟。

sentences.en: I, I would, my knee jerk response is to say more is better.
sentences.zh: 我，我下意识的反应是越多越好。

sentences.en: And I think you want to have enough time in the natural environment that you kind of feel like you're kind of away from your day to day.
sentences.zh: 我想你需要有足够的时间置身于自然环境中，让你觉得自己有点远离了日常生活。

sentences.en: But, you know, we do think that kind of, even if you only had five minutes, maybe listening to five minutes of nature sounds would have some benefit.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，我们确实认为，即使你只有五分钟，也许听五分钟的自然之声也会有一些益处。

sentences.en: But we do think the longer that you can interact with the nature, the better.
sentences.zh: 但我们确实认为，你接触大自然的时间越长越好。

sentences.en: Another thing that we don't really know is sort of like the cumulative effects.
sentences.zh: 另一件我们不太清楚的事情是累积效应。

sentences.en: So if you spend two hours in nature a week, you know, for 10 weeks in a row, how good is that?
sentences.zh: 所以如果你每周在大自然中待两个小时，你知道的，连续10周，效果会有多好？

sentences.en: And we don't know the answer to that in part because those are hard studies to do, but they're necessary studies that we need to do.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道这个问题的答案，部分原因是这些研究很难做，但它们又是我们需要去做得必要研究。

sentences.en: We just haven't done them yet as a field.
sentences.zh: 作为这个领域的研究人员，我们只是还没做过这些研究。

sentences.en: We're going to take a short break.
sentences.zh: 我们要休息一会儿。

sentences.en: When we return, we'll talk about whether you have to enjoy spending time in nature to benefit
sentences.zh: 当我们回来时，我们将讨论你是否必须喜欢在大自然中度过时光才能从中受益

sentences.en: from it and about whether it's helpful to bring natural elements like plants and nature scenes into your home.
sentences.zh: 以及将植物和自然风景等自然元素带入你的家中是否有帮助。

sentences.en: So a lot of people don't consider themselves particularly outdoorsy.
sentences.zh: 所以很多人并不认为自己特别喜欢户外活动。

sentences.en: Maybe they like taking a walk on a beautiful 70 degree day, but they want to stay inside when it's cold or raining.
sentences.zh: 也许他们喜欢在舒适的70度天气里散步，但天冷或下雨时他们就想待在室内。

sentences.en: Can you still get the benefits of nature, even if you're taking a walk in the rain and you're not really loving it?
sentences.zh: 即使你在雨中散步且并不是真的很喜欢它，你仍然可以获得大自然的益处吗？

sentences.en: Yes, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对可以。

sentences.en: I think this is one of the more counterintuitive findings.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是最反直觉的发现之一。

sentences.en: So everybody's, you know, says, oh, okay, Mark, you know, yeah, nature is good for us.
sentences.zh: 所以每个人都，你知道的，说，哦，好吧，马克，你知道的，对，大自然对我们有好处。

sentences.en: We like nature.
sentences.zh: 我们喜欢大自然。

sentences.en: So it's not a surprise that nature might improve, you know, attention and working memory.
sentences.zh: 所以大自然可能会改善，你知道的，注意力和工作记忆，这并不令人意外。

sentences.en: But what was really interesting from the walking study, the original walking study, is that we had people walk at different times of the year.
sentences.zh: 但散步研究，也就是最初的散步研究中真正有趣的是，我们让人们在一年中的不同时间进行散步。

sentences.en: So some people walked in June when it was around 80 degrees Fahrenheit in Ann Arbor.
sentences.zh: 所以有些人是在六月安娜堡气温大约华氏80度时散步的。

sentences.en: And people really loved the walk.
sentences.zh: 人们非常喜欢这次散步。

sentences.en: I said, Mark, I can't believe you're paying me to go for a walk in nature.
sentences.zh: 我说，马克，我真不敢相信你花钱让我去大自然中散步。

sentences.en: Loved the nature walk, showed really healthy attention and memory benefits.
sentences.zh: 他们非常喜欢自然散步，并表现出非常健康的注意力和记忆力收益。

sentences.en: We also had people walk in January when it was about 25 degrees Fahrenheit.
sentences.zh: 我们还让人们在一月份散步，当时气温约为华氏25度。

sentences.en: And people said, Mark, I did not like that walk.
sentences.zh: 人们说，马克，我一点也不喜欢那次散步。

sentences.en: I was freezing my butt off out there.
sentences.zh: 我在外面冻得屁股都快掉了。

sentences.en: They did not show mood benefits walking in January, but they showed the same memory and attention benefits as the people that walked in June.
sentences.zh: 他们在冬日散步时没有表现出情绪上的改善，但他们表现出了与六月散步的人相同的记忆力和注意力收益。

sentences.en: So you didn't even have to enjoy the nature walk to get these cognitive benefits.
sentences.zh: 所以你甚至不需要享受自然散步就能获得这些认知益处。

sentences.en: And I think that's really, really important that this isn't just about liking.
sentences.zh: 我认为这非常非常重要，这不仅仅是关于喜欢与否。

sentences.en: So it's not like, you know, oh, if I eat a piece of chocolate and it makes me a little happy that I'm going to get these cognitive benefits.
sentences.zh: 所以这不像是，你知道的，哦，如果我吃了一块巧克力，它让我有点快乐，我就会获得这些认知益处。

sentences.en: This is something else.
sentences.zh: 这是完全不同的东西。

sentences.en: This is something about how the environment, how the physical environment can sort of rest our directed attention independent of changes in mood.
sentences.zh: 这与环境有关，物理环境如何在不依赖情绪变化的情况下，让我们定向注意力得到休息。

sentences.en: And that can get a cognitive benefit, even if we don't really enjoy the walk in nature.
sentences.zh: 即使我们并不是真的很享受在大自然中的散步，也能获得认知上的益处。

sentences.en: I guess I would kind of say it's sort of like eating spinach or broccoli.
sentences.zh: 我想我可以说这有点像吃菠菜或西兰花。

sentences.en: You know, you might not think it tastes the best, but it's good for us.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你可能觉得它不是最好吃的，但它对我们有好处。

sentences.en: Now, I will say that there must be some kind of threshold.
sentences.zh: 现在，我要说的是，一定存在某种阈值。

sentences.en: And, you know, sometimes we have cheeky reviewers that read our papers and they say, well, what about a wildfire or what if you're being chased by a bear in nature?
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，有时我们会有一些爱挑剔的审稿人，他们阅读我们的论文并说，嗯，野火怎么样？或者如果在自然中被熊追呢？

sentences.en: And we'd say, of course, we don't think that's going to be restorative of attention because you're going to have to use a lot of directed attention.
sentences.zh: 我们会说，当然，我们不认为那会恢复注意力，因为你必须消耗大量的定向注意力。

sentences.en: So again, you know, if you're in nature and it's, you know, 10 degrees Fahrenheit and you're not wearing a proper coat or hat, it's not, we don't think it's going to be beneficial.
sentences.zh: 所以再说一次，你知道的，如果你在大自然中，温度是，你知道的，华氏10度，而且你没有穿合适的外套或戴帽子，这不会，我们认为这不会有益。

sentences.en: It's going to be too uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 这会太难受了。

sentences.en: But if your minimum level of comfort and needs have been met, you don't have to really enjoy the nature walk to get the benefit.
sentences.zh: 但如果你的最低舒适度和需求得到了满足，你就不必真的去享受自然散步也能获得益处。

sentences.en: That's interesting.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣。

sentences.en: Now, some people will use their daily walks to catch up on listening to podcasts or maybe they'll call a friend they've been meaning to talk to.
sentences.zh: 现在，有些人会利用每天的散步时间来听播客，或者他们会给一直想联系的朋友打电话。

sentences.en: Can you still get the same cognitive and other benefits of nature or do we need to unplug our devices to get the full benefit?
sentences.zh: 你还能获得大自然的认知及其他益处吗？还是我们需要拔掉设备的插头才能获得全部益处？

sentences.en: Yeah, unfortunately, I think you got to unplug and there's been some work that has shown that if you're talking on a cell phone while on the walk, you don't get the benefit.
sentences.zh: 是的，不幸的是，我认为你必须拔掉电子设备的插头，并且有一些研究表明，如果你在散步时打手机，你就无法获得这种益处。

sentences.en: And I think that makes sense because if you're listening to a podcast or if you're talking
sentences.zh: 我想这说得通，因为如果你在听播客，或者如果你在电话里和朋友说话

sentences.en: to a friend on the phone, you're having to use a lot of directed attention and you're also distracting yourself from the natural stimulation that we think is softly fascinating.
sentences.zh: 你必须使用大量的定向注意力，而且你也在分散自己的注意力，无法关注我们认为具有温和吸引力的自然刺激。

sentences.en: So we think it's really important that you actually unplug when you go into nature.
sentences.zh: 所以我们认为，当你进入大自然时，拔掉电子设备插头真的非常重要。

sentences.en: If you want to get the most bang for your buck, you want to allow all of your involuntary attention to be captured by the environment.
sentences.zh: 如果你想物有所值，你就得让环境捕捉你所有的非自主注意力。

sentences.en: And I would also advocate that you go for the walk by yourself.
sentences.zh: 我还主张你一个人去散步。

sentences.en: So for example, I have, I have kids and it's important for my kids to be out in nature, but when I take them out in nature, I don't count that as a nature break for me.
sentences.zh: 比如，我有，我有孩子，对我的孩子来说去大自然中玩耍很重要，但当我带他们去大自然时，我不认为那是我的自然休息时间。

sentences.en: That's for them.
sentences.zh: 那是为他们准备的。

sentences.en: Um, and, uh, I have to find time to, to go out on my own.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且，我必须找时间自己一个人出去。

sentences.en: Uh, I think it is really important to, to not have any other kinds of distraction or things like that, that are going to be requiring directed attention.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为真正重要的是不要有任何其他形式的分心或诸如此类需要消耗定向注意力的事情。

sentences.en: You want all of your involuntary attention to be kind of automatically captured by that natural stimulation.
sentences.zh: 你希望你所有的非自主注意力都能被那种自然刺激自动吸引。

sentences.en: A lot of people try to bring nature into their homes by decorating with plants or photos or paintings of natural scenes.
sentences.zh: 许多人试图通过用植物、照片或自然风景画来装饰，将大自然带入他们的家中。

sentences.en: And there's even a term for this biophilic design.
sentences.zh: 甚至还有一个专门的术语叫“亲生物设计”。

sentences.en: Is there research that shows that there are actual benefits from biophilic design and what kinds of decorating touches are we talking about here?
sentences.zh: 有没有研究表明亲生物设计确实能带来好处？我们这里指的是哪种装饰触感？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That's a really good question too.
sentences.zh: 这也是一个非常好的问题。

sentences.en: And, and yes, people have found benefits from bringing natural stimulation into their home environments, even if it's artificial.
sentences.zh: 而且，是的，人们发现将自然刺激引入家居环境（即使是人工的）也能带来益处。

sentences.en: So, you know, we kind of talk about different layers of these effects.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，我们讨论过这些影响的不同层次。

sentences.en: So the best thing is if you can go out into real nature, then like the second best thing is do you have a view, uh, to real nature that can be good.
sentences.zh: 所以最好的情况是如果你能去真正的自然中，其次最好的情况是，你是否能看到真实自然的风景，这也不错。

sentences.en: But if you don't have a view to real nature, you can bring maybe plants, real plants into your office.
sentences.zh: 但如果你看不到真实的自然风景，你也许可以在办公室里摆放植物，真正的植物。

sentences.en: But if you don't have good natural light, you can have fake plants.
sentences.zh: 但如果你没有良好的自然光，你可以养假植物。

sentences.en: So for example, I have a plant behind me right now in my office, that's a fake plant, uh, because I don't have good, uh, natural light in my office.
sentences.zh: 所以举个例子，我办公室现在身后就有一株植物，那是一株假植物，因为我办公室没有良好的自然光。

sentences.en: And people have found that, you know, in hospitals in different settings, having fake plants, fake greenery can have some of these same benefits.
sentences.zh: 人们发现，你知道的，在医院和其他不同的环境中，摆放假植物、假绿植可以带来其中一些相同的益处。

sentences.en: I don't know if studies about improving cognitive functioning with the artificial nature, but
sentences.zh: 我不知道是否有关于用人工自然改善认知功能的研究，但是

sentences.en: definitely improving mood, improving calmness, having even fake nature can be beneficial.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，改善情绪、增强平静感，即使是假的大自然也能受益。

sentences.en: And then you also brought up this idea of biophilic patterns.
sentences.zh: 然后你还提出了亲生物图案这个概念。

sentences.en: So people have talked about, you know, mimicking the patterns of nature.
sentences.zh: 所以人们一直在讨论，你知道的，模仿大自然的图案。

sentences.en: So you can imagine carpet that has, uh, some of the curved edge kind of structure of nature,
sentences.zh: 所以你可以想象地毯具有大自然的那种弧形边缘结构，

sentences.en: but doesn't, uh, actually isn't actually overtly nature.
sentences.zh: 但没有，嗯，实际上并不是那种一眼就能看出来的自然风貌。

sentences.en: And people have found that even that can have some benefits.
sentences.zh: 人们发现，即使是这样也能带来一些益处。

sentences.en: And, and we've found that too, with some research on how, um, interacting with nature can change what people think about.
sentences.zh: 我们通过关于与大自然互动如何改变人们想法的研究也发现了这一点。

sentences.en: So we did a study, um, with a private foundation, uh, that was called the TKF foundation.
sentences.zh: 所以我们和一家私人基金会做过一项研究，这个基金会叫做TKF基金会。

sentences.en: Now it's called nature sacred.
sentences.zh: 现在它叫自然神圣（Nature Sacred）。

sentences.en: And this foundation built, uh, like 150 parks, uh, mostly in the, uh, Baltimore, Washington,
sentences.zh: 这个基金会建造了大约150个公园，主要在巴尔的摩、华盛顿、

sentences.en: DC, Annapolis, Maryland area.
sentences.zh: 哥伦比亚特区和马里兰州安纳波利斯地区。

sentences.en: And, uh, all of these parks had a characteristic bench, a TKF bench that they called it, that had a journal entry underneath, a journal, a diary, sorry.
sentences.zh: 而且，所有这些公园都有一个标志性的长椅，他们称之为TKF长椅，长椅下面有一个日志条目，一本日志，抱歉，是日记。

sentences.en: And people could write, uh, journal entries, uh, and when they're sitting in the, in the park and this foundation actually transcribed all of these, uh, journal entries.
sentences.zh: 人们坐在公园里时可以写日记，而且这个基金会实际上把所有这些日记条目都转录了下来。

sentences.en: So there are about 12,000 journal entries from people sitting in these parks and just writing about what they were thinking about.
sentences.zh: 所以大约有12,000条日记，来自坐在这些公园里并写下他们想法的人们。

sentences.en: And what we were interested in was to see, do different elements of these parks impact what people write about?
sentences.zh: 我们感兴趣的是看看这些公园的不同元素是否会影响人们书写的内容？

sentences.en: And so the foundation also had pictures from these parks.
sentences.zh: 因此，该基金会还保留了这些公园的照片。

sentences.en: And so with my student, Kate shirts, we actually quantify different things from these images of the parks and also quantified what people were writing about.
sentences.zh: 所以我和我的学生凯特·舍茨（Kate Schertz）一起，实际上量化了这些公园图片中的不同内容，同时也量化了人们所写的内容。

sentences.en: So first I'll start with what's contained in the park.
sentences.zh: 所以首先我从公园里包含的内容开始讲起。

sentences.en: So one of the first things that Kate did was, you know, we had pictures from all these parks and Kate just had people, a different group of participants.
sentences.zh: 所以凯特做的第一件事之一就是，你知道的，我们有所有这些公园的照片，凯特让人们，即另一组参与者。

sentences.en: So these online participants just rate the pictures from these parks for how natural they thought the parks were.
sentences.zh: 这些在线参与者只需对这些公园的照片进行评分，评估他们认为这些公园有多自然。

sentences.en: And some of the parks, you know, were in kind of a more urban-y kind of area and had more of an urban feel, even though they were a park.
sentences.zh: 其中一些公园，你知道的，位于更偏都市化的区域，具有更多的城市气息，尽管它们是个公园。

sentences.en: And some felt like you were in more of a secluded natural environment.
sentences.zh: 而另一些则让人感觉你身处更隐蔽的自然环境中。

sentences.en: So it felt more, more natural.
sentences.zh: 所以感觉更加自然。

sentences.en: And then what Kate did is she did something called topic modeling, which is a way that you can convert text into something quantifiable.
sentences.zh: 然后凯特做的是她做了一件叫做主题建模的事情，这是一种可以将文本转换为可量化内容的方法。

sentences.en: So she, she ran a topic model that kind of broke down, uh, all these 12,000 journal entries into 10 topics.
sentences.zh: 所以她运行了一个主题模型，将这所有12,000条日记拆解成了10个主题。

sentences.en: And then what, uh, Kate could do was then say for each journal, journal entry, how much did it relate, uh, to this topic?
sentences.zh: 然后凯特可以做的是，针对每一篇日记，说明它与这个主题的关联度有多高？

sentences.en: And so one of the topics that we found was related to nature, that people were writing about things related to nature.
sentences.zh: 我们发现其中一个主题与自然有关，人们在写与自然相关的事情。

sentences.en: Um, and he said something like tree or bird or things like that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且他说了一些类似于树木或鸟类之类的话。

sentences.en: And one of the first sanity checks we found is that when people were in parks that were rated as more natural, they tended to write more about topics related to naturalness.
sentences.zh: 我们发现的第一个健全性检查之一是，当人们身处被评为更自然的公园时，他们往往会写更多与自然度相关的主题。

sentences.en: So that was a good sanity check and pretty interesting.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个很好的健全性检查，而且非常有趣。

sentences.en: And even wilder thing was, is that Kate also used some computer vision algorithms to quantify
sentences.zh: 更疯狂的是，凯特还使用了一些计算机视觉算法来量化

sentences.en: in these different parks, how many curved edges or curved, uh, lines were in these parks.
sentences.zh: 在这些不同的公园里，有多少弧形边缘或弧形线条。

sentences.en: And she found that if the park had more curved lines and it are curved edges, people were more likely to write about topics related to spirit, spirituality and their life journey.
sentences.zh: 她发现，如果公园有更多的弧形线条和弧形边缘，人们更有可能写关于精神、灵性和他们的人生旅程的主题。

sentences.en: So that was pretty interesting, but very correlational.
sentences.zh: 这相当有趣，但非常具有相关性。

sentences.en: You know, again, we're not manipulating anything, but then what Kate did was as she ran another
sentences.zh: 你知道的，再次强调，我们没有操纵任何东西，但接着凯特做的是她进行了另一项研究

sentences.en: study where she manipulated the amount of curved edges that were in pictures that people were looking at and then had participants pick what topic went with the image.
sentences.zh: 其中她操纵了人们正在观看的图片中弧形边缘的数量，然后让参与者选择与图像相匹配的主题。

sentences.en: And if the image had more curved edges, people were more likely to pick the topic that was related to spirituality in their life journey.
sentences.zh: 如果图像有更多的弧形边缘，人们更有可能选择与灵性和他们的人生旅程相关的主题。

sentences.en: So that was experimental, but then it got even crazier where she scrambled the scene.
sentences.zh: 所以这是实验性的，但随后变得更加疯狂，她打乱了场景。

sentences.en: So now you like take this image of nature and you've got all the edges so you can see the trees, but then she scrambles the edges.
sentences.zh: 所以现在你拿这张自然图像，所有的边缘都被打乱了，所以你可以看到树木，但她把边缘打乱了。

sentences.en: So you can't tell what it is anymore.
sentences.zh: 所以你再也认不出它是什么了。

sentences.en: It's got all the edges in there, but they're all scrambled up, kind of looks like a Jackson
sentences.zh: 里面有所有的边缘，但它们都被打乱了，看起来有点像杰克逊·波洛克的画作。

sentences.en: Pollock painting.
sentences.zh: 波洛克画作。

sentences.en: And what Kate found was that even in these scrambled images, if they had more curved edges in them, people, it caused people to think more about spirituality in their life journey.
sentences.zh: 凯特发现，即使在这些打乱的图像中，如果它们包含更多的弧形边缘，人们也会更多地思考灵性和他们的人生旅程。

sentences.en: So that was a very sort of circuitous route to basically say that if you have curved edges, biophilic kind of architecture in your home or in your carpeting or on your wallpaper,
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个非常曲折的过程，基本上是想说明，如果你家里、地毯上或壁纸上有弧形边缘、亲生物的建筑风格，

sentences.en: it might cause you to think more about topics related to spirituality in your life journey.
sentences.zh: 它可能会促使你更多地思考与灵性和人生旅程相关的主题。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: That's pretty amazing.
sentences.zh: 这太神奇了。

sentences.en: Quite an experiment.
sentences.zh: 真是个不错的实验。

sentences.en: Has this research changed the choices you've made in your own life, like in terms of where you live or how you spend your free time?
sentences.zh: 这项研究有没有改变你现实生活中的选择，比如你居住的地方，或者你如何度过闲暇时间？

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 嗯，绝对有。

sentences.en: So we, we perfectly chose, we bought a house that was close to two nature trails, even though
sentences.zh: 所以我们，我们仔细挑选过，我们买了一栋离两条自然步道很近的房子，尽管

sentences.en: maybe it was a little bit of a smaller house compared to another house that we could have bought that would have been bigger, but it would have been not so close to these nature
sentences.zh: 比起我们本可以买到的另一栋面积更大但离这些自然步道不够近、

sentences.en: trails and also closer to more car traffic.
sentences.zh: 而且离汽车车流更近的房子，这栋房子可能稍微小了一点。

sentences.en: So we were very cognizant about that.
sentences.zh: 所以我们对这一点非常清楚。

sentences.en: We definitely have brought more real plants into our, our home.
sentences.zh: 我们确实在家里摆放了更多真正的植物。

sentences.en: So we have a big bay window in the front of our house and we have some big plants, uh, there, uh, as I mentioned before, in my office, I don't have good natural light, but I have
sentences.zh: 所以在我们房子的正前方有一个很大的凸窗，那里有一些很大的植物，呃，正如我之前提到的，在我的办公室里，我没有很好的自然光，但我有

sentences.en: fake plants in my office.
sentences.zh: 假植物在我办公室里。

sentences.en: And then also too, when I'm working, if I feel like I'm getting kind of mentally fatigued,
sentences.zh: 而且还有，当我工作时，如果我觉得自己有点精神疲劳，

sentences.en: I don't scroll the internet or serve the internet or scroll my, well, I don't even have social media, I don't get on my cell phone.
sentences.zh: 我不会刷网页或浏览互联网，或者刷我的，好吧，我甚至没有社交媒体，我不会玩手机。

sentences.en: I try to go out and go for a walk in nature.
sentences.zh: 我试着出去到大自然中散步。

sentences.en: Um, and I think I know, again, I have the luxury, you know, my schedule is pretty flexible that I can do that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想我知道，再次强调，我很奢侈，你知道，我的时间安排相当灵活，我可以做到这一点。

sentences.en: But I think this is important for people to consider that, um, when you are feeling mentally fatigued, it's not always such a good idea to try to power through.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得大家有必要考虑这一点，嗯，当你感到精神疲劳时，硬撑着往往并不是一个好主意。

sentences.en: It might be a better idea to try to take a break.
sentences.zh: 休息一下可能是一个更好的主意。

sentences.en: And the kind of break that we think is going to be, uh, really beneficial is a break in nature.
sentences.zh: 而我们认为会非常受益的那种休息，就是在大自然中休息。

sentences.en: What are the implications of this research for policymakers and urban planners and other people who make decisions that shape, uh, towns, cities, neighborhoods, and does the
sentences.zh: 这项研究对政策制定者、城市规划者以及其他负责塑造城镇、城市、社区面貌的决策者有什么启示，而且，

sentences.en: trend toward these mixed use developments, which are kind of a big thing where I happen to live, or is that a good thing or a bad thing based on, you know, the research that
sentences.zh: 向这种混合用途开发的趋势——这在我住的地方算是一件大事——根据你所做的研究，这究竟是件好事还是坏事呢？

sentences.en: you've done first, I just want to say, we don't think cities are bad.
sentences.zh: 首先，我只想说，我们并不是觉得城市不好。

sentences.en: We think cities are really good.
sentences.zh: 我们觉得城市真的很好。

sentences.en: So I wouldn't want anybody to take this research and say, oh, okay, let's all move out of cities and go, uh, into more rural kind of areas.
sentences.zh: 所以我可不希望任何人把这项研究断章取义，然后说，哦，好吧，那我们都搬出城市，去，呃，更偏远的乡村地区吧。

sentences.en: No, we think cities are good for a number of reasons.
sentences.zh: 不，我们认为城市在很多方面都很好。

sentences.en: Um, in fact, we've done research to show that more populated cities have lower rates of depression per capita, uh, more populated cities, larger cities have lower implicit racial
sentences.zh: 嗯，事实上，我们做过的研究表明，人口更密集的城市人均抑郁率更低，呃，人口更密集、规模更大的城市，其潜在的种族

sentences.en: biases, you know, so cities are great, but we want to incorporate, want to bring more nature into cities.
sentences.zh: 偏见也更低，你知道的，所以城市很棒，但我们希望将更多的大自然融入城市。

sentences.en: So we want cities to have more parks and those parks have to be accessible and they have to be safe.
sentences.zh: 所以我们希望城市有更多的公园，而且这些公园必须交通便利，必须安全。

sentences.en: So we've done some studies in Chicago where we had, you know, high school and college students kind of go around their neighborhood and take pictures of parks in their neighborhood
sentences.zh: 因此我们在芝加哥做了一些研究，让高中生和大学生在他们的社区四处走走，拍摄他们社区公园的照片，

sentences.en: and also answer some questions about parks in their neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 并回答一些关于他们社区公园的问题。

sentences.en: And we found that in Chicago, many of the parks in the lower resource neighborhoods, these students did not feel safe, uh, in those spaces.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，在芝加哥，资源较少社区的许多公园，这些学生在那些空间里并不感到安全。

sentences.en: So it's not just enough to have the park, people have to feel safe in the park.
sentences.zh: 所以仅仅拥有公园是不够的，人们必须在公园里感到安全。

sentences.en: And so we need to do all that we can to make sure that people are feeling safe and that there's
sentences.zh: 因此，我们需要尽一切努力确保人们有安全感，并且有

sentences.en: good lighting and that these parks are well, well maintained, uh, to get, to get the benefit.
sentences.zh: 良好的照明，而且这些公园必须得到良好的维护，才能，才能发挥作用。

sentences.en: So it's not enough just to have the park.
sentences.zh: 所以仅仅拥有公园是不够的。

sentences.en: People need to feel, feel safe in the park.
sentences.zh: 人们需要在公园里感到安全。

sentences.en: And then, you know, there's a lot of things too.
sentences.zh: 还有，你知道，也有很多其他的事情。

sentences.en: So I don't want to pick on Chicago too much, but Chicago has these fantastic parks, um, right
sentences.zh: 所以我不想太针对芝加哥，但芝加哥有这些绝佳的公园，嗯，就在

sentences.en: by the University of Chicago campus, Jackson park, the midway place, and Washington park.
sentences.zh: 芝加哥大学校园旁边，杰克逊公园、中途地带以及华盛顿公园。

sentences.en: These parks were designed by Frederick Law Olmstead, the same landscape architect who designed
sentences.zh: 这些公园是由弗雷德里克·劳·奥姆斯特德设计的，他也是纽约
zh_words: 弗雷德里克·劳·奥姆斯特德

sentences.en: central park in New York, but the park, these parks in Chicago do not have the same effect as central park in New York.
sentences.zh: 中央公园的景观设计师，但芝加哥的这些公园并没有发挥出与纽约中央公园相同的效果。

sentences.en: And I think part of the reason for that is that there's really a lot of car traffic that is, uh, right next to these parks.
sentences.zh: 我想部分原因在于，紧挨着这些公园确实有非常多的汽车流量。

sentences.en: And I remember taking my kids one time walking to Jackson park by this garden, Jackson park
sentences.zh: 我记得有一次带着我的孩子们步行去杰克逊公园，路过杰克逊公园的这个花园，

sentences.en: called the circle garden, which isn't there anymore because they've built the Obama library.
sentences.zh: 叫做环形花园，现在已经不在了，因为那里建了奥巴马图书馆。

sentences.en: And it's a, it, the circle garden was a really beautiful part of a Jackson park.
sentences.zh: 这是一个，它，环形花园曾经是杰克逊公园非常美丽的一部分。

sentences.en: And as I'm walking with my kids in, in Jackson park, literally a car was zooming by on the nearby street and a hubcap flew off of the car and just spun around in front of us.
sentences.zh: 正当我带着孩子们在杰克逊公园散步时，一辆汽车呼啸着从旁边的街道上开过，一个轮毂盖从车上飞了下来，就在我们面前转圈。

sentences.en: And I remember thinking, this is just such a shame when we have this great park here, but because of the car traffic and the noise, it's just not having the same effect as if
sentences.zh: 我记得当时想，我们这里有这么棒的一个公园，但由于车流和噪音，它竟然没有达到如果我们

sentences.en: we, if we could remove that car traffic.
sentences.zh: 能够消除这些车流时所应有的效果，这真是太遗憾了。

sentences.en: So I think again, too, so we, the parks need to be safe, but they also have to be secluded.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得同样，我们需要公园既安全，但它们也必须清幽。

sentences.en: Well, a lot of this urban stimulation that we think is taxing directed attention.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这种都市刺激很大程度上消耗了我们的定向注意力。

sentences.en: Um, so I, so that's, I think something that urban planners also have to have to think about.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以，我认为这也是城市规划者必须考虑的问题。

sentences.en: Um, and then, you know, there's lots of creative things that we can do.
sentences.zh: 嗯，然后，你知道，我们可以做很多有创意的事情。

sentences.en: For example, like imagine the skyscrapers in our cities, if they had like vines growing all the way down them, or if we had trees kind of growing out of the top of these buildings,
sentences.zh: 例如，想象一下我们城市的摩天大楼，如果它们的墙面爬满了藤蔓，或者如果这些建筑的顶部长出树木，

sentences.en: or, you know, there's a lot of creative things that we can do to try to put more nature, uh, into our cities.
sentences.zh: 或者，你知道，我们可以做很多有创意的事情，试图把更多的自然，呃，融入我们的城市。

sentences.en: And, and I think that's something that we really, uh, want, want people to think about.
sentences.zh: 而且，我认为这是我们真正，呃，希望人们去思考的事情。

sentences.en: And even another thing too, is that the architecture, so we've done studies where architecture that's more biophilic, that mimics more of the patterns of nature.
sentences.zh: 还有一件事，那就是建筑，我们做过研究，更具亲生物性的建筑会模仿更多自然的规律。

sentences.en: So you can imagine Gaudi buildings in Barcelona, or even on the university of Chicago campus,
sentences.zh: 所以你可以想象巴塞罗那的高迪建筑，甚至在芝加哥大学校园里，

sentences.en: we have this beautiful Gothic architecture that has all these, uh, curves to it that mimics patterns of nature.
sentences.zh: 我们有美丽的哥特式建筑，带有各种各样的弧线，模仿了大自然的图案。

sentences.en: We actually find that people really prefer that kind of architecture and they actually see nature in that architecture, even though there is no overt nature in it.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上发现人们非常喜欢这种建筑，而且他们确实能在这种建筑中看到大自然，尽管里面并没有公开的自然元素。

sentences.en: Um, now building in that way might be more expensive, but if it leads to these potential cognitive benefits, maybe it would, um, it would be worth it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，用这种方式建造可能成本更高，但如果它能带来这些潜在的认知益处，也许它，嗯，会是值得的。

sentences.en: So I think that's, that's really important to think about too, you know, versus some of the architecture that's around us.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得，与我们周围那些非常粗野主义、只有直线条的建筑相比，这一点确实也非常重要。

sentences.en: That's very, you know, brutalist that just has, you know, straight lines.
sentences.zh: 非常，你知道的，野兽派风格的建筑，只有直线条。

sentences.en: And we find people don't really like that kind of architecture.
sentences.zh: 我们发现人们其实并不喜欢那种建筑。

sentences.en: So again, this, this is beyond landscape architects, but even actual architects that are building
sentences.zh: 所以说，这不仅超越了景观设计师的范畴，甚至连建造

sentences.en: the actual structures, if they can incorporate more of these biophilic designs into their architecture, we think that can have benefits too.
sentences.zh: 实际结构的建筑师，如果他们能在建筑中融入更多这些亲生物设计，我们认为这也会带来好处。

sentences.en: So just to wrap up, what, what's next for you?
sentences.zh: 那么总结一下，你接下来要做什么？

sentences.en: What are you working on now?
sentences.zh: 你现在在研究什么？

sentences.en: What are the big questions you want to answer?
sentences.zh: 你想解答的重大问题是什么？

sentences.en: So I think we definitely want to start getting direct brain measurements of people interacting with nature.
sentences.zh: 所以我想我们肯定想开始获取人们与自然互动时的直接大脑测量数据。

sentences.en: Um, so that's what we're doing with FNIRS now where we've started to collect data from
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是我们现在用功能性近红外光谱技术（fNIRS）正在做的事情，我们已经开始收集

sentences.en: about 20 people who have been walking in more natural environments versus more urban environments while wearing this FNIRS device.
sentences.zh: 大约20人的数据，他们在佩戴fNIRS设备的同时，在更自然的自然环境中与更具都市感的环境中散步。

sentences.en: And we want to see, um, if them, what are the changes in the brain, uh, that are occurring when people are walking in, in real nature versus, um, more built environments.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看，呃，当人们在真实的自然环境中散步与在，呃，更多人工建造的环境中散步时，大脑究竟发生了什么变化。

sentences.en: We've also become very interested to try to quantify what does soft fascination really mean?
sentences.zh: 我们也开始对量化“柔和吸引力”到底意味着什么产生浓厚兴趣。

sentences.en: So we've started to look at thousands of nature and urban images, um, and analyzing them with a, with a JPEG compression kind of algorithm.
sentences.zh: 所以我们开始研究数以千计的自然和城市图像，嗯，并用一种JPEG压缩算法来分析它们。

sentences.en: So JPEG compression is a means that our computers and our phones use to try to lower the amount of memory that images take up.
sentences.zh: 因此，JPEG压缩是我们的电脑和手机用来试图减少图像占用内存空间的一种手段。

sentences.en: So for example, you know, let's say we have an image, uh, that's a hundred megabytes.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，你知道，假设我们有一张，呃，有一百兆字节的图像。

sentences.en: Oftentimes what our computers, uh, and what our phones will do is compress that image down into fewer bits.
sentences.zh: 通常我们的电脑，呃，还有我们的手机会做的是将该图像压缩成更少的比特。

sentences.en: And usually what that requires is kind of throwing away some information, like throwing away some
sentences.zh: 通常这需要丢弃一些信息，比如丢弃一些

sentences.en: of the little fine grained details and to our human eye, we can't tell any difference, but it saves a lot of room on our, uh, computers and on our phones.
sentences.zh: 非常精细的细节，而对于我们的肉眼来说，我们看不出任何区别，但它为我们的，呃，电脑和手机节省了大量的空间。

sentences.en: And we've been wondering, is it possible that nature scenes get compressed down into fewer bits than urban scenes?
sentences.zh: 我们在想，自然场景会不会比城市场景被压缩成更少的比特？

sentences.en: And it turns out that yes, that's true.
sentences.zh: 结果证明，是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: So nature scenes, the more natural the scene is, we're finding that it gets reduced to, to fewer bits compared to urban scenes.
sentences.zh: 所以自然场景，场景越自然，我们发现与城市场景相比，它被约简到的比特数就越少。

sentences.en: And maybe our brain is doing something similar related to that.
sentences.zh: 也许我们的大脑也在做类似的事情。

sentences.en: We've also had people tested people's memory of nature, urban scenes.
sentences.zh: 我们还测试了人们对自然和城市场景的记忆。

sentences.en: So we show them a bunch of different images and then ask them later, do you remember this image or not?
sentences.zh: 所以我们给他们展示一堆不同的图像，然后过一会儿问他们，你还记得这张图像吗？

sentences.en: Did you see this image or not?
sentences.zh: 你见过这张图像吗？

sentences.en: And it turns out people have better memory for the more urban scenes than they do for the more natural scenes.
sentences.zh: 结果证明，人们对城市场景的记忆比对自然场景的记忆更好。

sentences.en: And you might think, well, Mark, that sounds like a bad thing, but we think it's a good thing.
sentences.zh: 你可能会想，嗯，马克，这听起来像是一件坏事，但我们认为这是一件好事。

sentences.en: And we think it means that when people see the nature scene, they're not processing it as deeply and then they're not remembering it.
sentences.zh: 我们认为这意味着当人们看到自然场景时，他们没有对其进行那么深度的处理，因此也没有记住它。

sentences.en: And so maybe it's sort of means that it's easier for our brains to process.
sentences.zh: 所以也许这某种程度上意味着我们的大脑处理起来更容易。

sentences.en: So, so that's been kind of cool.
sentences.zh: 所以，所以这挺酷的。

sentences.en: And then to kind of bring it together, we're finding that part of the reason why nature scenes are less memorable is because they're more compressible.
sentences.zh: 然后总的来说，我们发现自然场景之所以不那么令人难忘，部分原因在于它们的可压缩性更高。

sentences.en: So part of the reason why you don't remember the nature scenes as much is because they're
sentences.zh: 所以你记不住自然场景的部分原因是因为它们被

sentences.en: more compressed down that you, that more information is thrown away and suggesting that maybe our
sentences.zh: 压缩得更厉害了，更多的信息被丢弃了，这表明也许我们的大脑正在对这些自然场景进行某种类似JPEG的压缩。

sentences.en: brains are doing some kind of JPEG like compression on these, on these nature scenes.
sentences.zh: 这太迷人了。

sentences.en: That's pretty fascinating.
sentences.zh: 太迷人了。

sentences.en: Well, Dr. Berman, I want to thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 好的，伯曼博士，我要感谢你今天能来参加。

sentences.zh: 我觉得这次交流真的非常有趣。

sentences.zh: 我希望我们的听众也觉得很有趣，并且在听完你的分享后能出去到大自然中走一走。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对的。
